records.name: Yucatan
records.summary:
Yucatan is not among the six Mexican states whose legislatures have enacted no legal gender-recognition procedure, per Human Rights Watch's March 2025 count (22 of 32 states have legislated one).

No Yucatan-specific ordinance, incident series or enforcement pattern against transgender people is supported by the surviving sources; the national criminal and human-rights framework applies in the state as elsewhere in Mexico.

records.name: Zacatecas
records.summary:
Zacatecas is not among the six Mexican states whose legislatures have enacted no legal gender-recognition procedure, per Human Rights Watch's March 2025 count (22 of 32 states have legislated one).

No Zacatecas-specific ordinance, incident series or enforcement pattern targeting transgender people appears in the surviving sources; Mexico's national criminal law and gender-recognition regime apply here as elsewhere in the country.

records.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
records.summary: No province-specific trans law, enforcement pattern or official statement was found: criminal law and the federal human-rights framework apply uniformly, and the province has no facility or expression rule differing from the national position. Police-reported hate crime across all motivations is the lowest in the country alongside Manitoba (5.3 per 100,000 in 2024); a +51% rise that year was from very small absolute numbers. Risk assessed at parity with the national picture.

records.name: Prince Edward Island
records.summary: No province-specific trans law, incident pattern, official statement or rate deviation was found. Federal criminal law and human-rights protection apply uniformly; the island has no facility, expression or registration rule differing from the national position. Risk assessed at parity with the national picture; as in all of Canada, no systematic count of trans deaths exists to measure outcomes here specifically.

records.name: Nova Scotia
records.summary: No province-specific trans law or hostile official pattern was found; federal criminal law and the federal human-rights framework apply uniformly. Halifax hosts a large, organised 2SLGBTQ+ community and institutional support (the national LGBT charity Egale Canada is based there), while the documented Canadian hostility pattern elsewhere concentrates in other provinces' school-board and library politics. Outside the capital, expect the rural small-town profile national surveys find worse for trans and non-binary people. Risk broadly at parity with the national picture.

records.name: Quebec
records.summary:
Quebec's recorded profile rests on the national data series: Statistics Canada's March 2026 release on police-reported hate crime (2024 data) shows gender-identity/expression-motivated incidents rising nationally for a fourth consecutive year — +8% to 139, nearly triple 2020 — and identifies no trans-specific provincial pattern for Quebec.

No Quebec-specific anti-trans legislation, ordinance or incident series appears in the surviving sources, alongside national NGO analysis of the same police data; the province's largest city anchors one of the country's most established organised 2SLGBTQ+ communities.

records.name: Ontario
records.summary:
No province-specific anti-trans statute, policy or official hostility is on record: while two other provinces have legislated restrictions on trans names, pronouns or care, Ontario's government has not.

Criminal law and human-rights protection operate federally and uniformly. The national police-reported hate-crime series (Statistics Canada, March 2026) shows gender-identity/expression-motivated incidents rising nationally — +8% to 139 in 2024, a fourth consecutive increase — without identifying a trans-specific provincial pattern for Ontario.

records.name: Manitoba
records.summary:
No province-specific trans law, incident series or official statement is on record for Manitoba; criminal law and human-rights protection apply uniformly from the federal level.

The province's capital hosts its organised community. The national police-reported hate-crime series (Statistics Canada, March 2026) records gender-identity/expression-motivated incidents rising nationally to 139 in 2024 (+8%, a fourth consecutive annual increase) and identifies no trans-specific provincial pattern for Manitoba.
